title: Discoveries
subtitle: Who found it first
about: Landmark discoveries from Aristarchus to gravitational waves, weighted towards physics. Each card names who did it, and the notes flag credit that was shared, disputed or overlooked.

cards.prompt: Proposed the first known model with the Sun, not the Earth, at the centre of the universe
cards.note: His treatise is lost; we know of his Sun-centred model mainly through a passage in Archimedes' The Sand Reckoner.

cards.prompt: Stated that an immersed body is buoyed up by a force equal to the weight of fluid displaced
cards.note: The Eureka bath story comes from Vitruvius, writing two centuries later, and in it the water measures volume, not buoyancy.

cards.prompt: Estimated the Earth's circumference from noon shadows at Syene and Alexandria
cards.note: Admirers nicknamed him Pentathlos, an all-rounder; critics called him Beta, because he supposedly came second in every field.

cards.prompt: Discovered the precession of the equinoxes by comparing his star positions with older records
cards.note: He compiled the first known comprehensive star catalogue in the West, yet only one of his fourteen or more books survives.

cards.prompt: Argued from experiment that vision happens when light enters the eye, in his Book of Optics
cards.note: Legend says he feigned madness to escape the caliph al-Hakim and wrote the book while kept under house arrest in Cairo.

cards.prompt: Published a detailed Sun-centred model of the planets in De revolutionibus
cards.note: An unsigned preface, added without authorisation by the preacher Andreas Osiander, presented the theory as a mere calculating device.

cards.prompt: Corrected Galen's anatomy in De humani corporis fabrica, drawing on human dissection
cards.note: He showed Galen had relied on animals: humans lack the rete mirabile, a network of blood vessels found in sheep.

cards.prompt: Argued in De Magnete that the Earth itself is a giant magnet
cards.note: He coined the Latin electricus, meaning like amber, from which the English word electricity was later derived.

cards.prompt: Showed that Mars moves in an ellipse, with the Sun at one focus
cards.note: An eight arcminute misfit between Tycho Brahe's data and his best circular model, he wrote, would lead to the reform of astronomy.

cards.prompt: Discovered four moons orbiting Jupiter with his telescope
cards.note: Simon Marius saw them independently at nearly the same time, and it is his names, Io, Europa, Ganymede and Callisto, that stuck.

cards.prompt: Demonstrated that the heart pumps blood around the body in a continuous circulation
cards.note: After he published De Motu Cordis, hostile physicians attacked him and, as a contemporary put it, he fell mightily in his practice.

cards.prompt: Invented the mercury barometer, showing that air pressure holds up a column of mercury
cards.note: He wrote to Michelangelo Ricci in 1644 that we live submerged at the bottom of an ocean of air.

cards.prompt: Published the law that the pressure of a gas is inversely proportional to its volume
cards.note: Richard Towneley and Henry Power noticed the relationship first; Boyle's assistant Robert Hooke probably built the apparatus.

cards.prompt: Coined the biological term cell, in his illustrated microscopy book Micrographia
cards.note: The compartments reminded him of monks' cells in a monastery; Samuel Pepys sat up until two in the morning reading the book.

cards.prompt: Showed with prisms that white light is a mixture of colours that can be recombined
cards.note: A bitter dispute with Robert Hooke over this work led Newton to delay publishing his Opticks until after Hooke died in 1703.

cards.prompt: Showed that light travels at a finite speed, by timing eclipses of Jupiter's moon Io
cards.note: He estimated light takes about 22 minutes to cross Earth's orbit; Cassini, his observatory director, never fully accepted the idea.

cards.prompt: First observed single-celled organisms, his animalcules, through microscopes he made himself
cards.note: A Delft draper who wanted to inspect thread, he kept his lens-making method secret, and it remained unknown for centuries.

cards.prompt: Published the three laws of motion and the law of universal gravitation
cards.note: The Principia was printed at Edmond Halley's expense, after Halley visited Newton in 1684 to ask about the inverse-square law.

cards.prompt: Predicted that the comet of 1682 would return in 1758
cards.note: Halley died in 1742; the comet was first spotted on Christmas Day 1758 by Johann Palitzsch, a German farmer and amateur astronomer.

cards.prompt: Proposed experiments showing lightning is electrical, famously flying a kite in a thunderstorm
cards.note: Thomas-François Dalibard performed Franklin's proposed experiment in France in May 1752, before the kite flight Priestley later described.

cards.prompt: Identified hydrogen as a distinct substance, an inflammable air that forms water when burned
cards.note: Cavendish called it inflammable air; Antoine Lavoisier later reproduced the experiment and gave the element its modern name.

cards.prompt: First to publish the isolation of oxygen, which he called dephlogisticated air
cards.note: Carl Wilhelm Scheele isolated it in Uppsala in 1773 or earlier but published later; Lavoisier first recognised it as an element.

cards.prompt: Explained combustion as combination with oxygen, overturning the phlogiston theory
cards.note: A tax farmer under the old regime, he was guillotined in 1794; the French government exonerated him a year and a half later.

cards.prompt: Discovered the planet Uranus from his garden in Bath, with a homemade telescope
cards.note: A professional musician who composed 24 symphonies, Herschel at first reported the new object as a comet.

cards.prompt: Used a torsion balance to establish the inverse-square law of force between electric charges
cards.note: Priestley and John Robison had suspected an inverse-square law earlier, and Henry Cavendish found it too but never published.

cards.prompt: Argued that slow, continuing processes shape the Earth over immense spans of time
cards.note: At Siccar Point in 1788, his companion John Playfair said the mind seemed to grow giddy looking so far into time.

cards.prompt: Showed that inoculation with cowpox protects against smallpox, pioneering vaccination
cards.note: Dorset farmer Benjamin Jesty had protected his own family with cowpox in 1774; Jenner's first subject was his gardener's son.

cards.prompt: Measured the gravitational attraction between lead spheres in a laboratory, finding the Earth's density
cards.note: The torsion balance was designed by John Michell, who died before using it; G itself never appears in Cavendish's paper.

cards.prompt: Built the first electric battery, a pile of metal discs separated by brine-soaked cloth
cards.note: It grew out of his argument with Luigi Galvani over frogs' legs; Volta also discovered methane in the marshes of Lake Maggiore.

cards.prompt: Showed that light can interfere with itself, reviving the wave theory against Newton's corpuscles
cards.note: It is unclear which experiments he actually performed; the same polymath also helped decipher Egyptian hieroglyphs on the Rosetta Stone.

cards.prompt: Proposed that each element is made of identical atoms with a characteristic relative weight
cards.note: He gave the first scientific description of colour blindness; tests on his preserved eyeball in 1995 showed he had deuteranopia.

cards.prompt: Proposed that equal volumes of gases, at the same temperature and pressure, contain equal numbers of molecules
cards.note: The idea won acceptance only after Stanislao Cannizzaro championed it at the Karlsruhe Congress in 1860, four years after Avogadro's death.

cards.prompt: Systematically mapped and measured the dark lines in the spectrum of sunlight
cards.note: William Hyde Wollaston first noticed some dark lines in 1802; Fraunhofer rediscovered them independently and measured their wavelengths.

cards.prompt: Showed that an electric current deflects a nearby compass needle, linking electricity and magnetism
cards.note: Tales of a lucky accident in mid-lecture oversimplify; he had been seeking a link between electricity and magnetism for years.

cards.prompt: Showed that the maximum efficiency of a heat engine depends only on its hot and cold temperatures
cards.note: His only publication, printed at his own expense, attracted little attention in his lifetime; he died of cholera aged 36.

cards.prompt: Synthesised urea, an organic compound, from inorganic starting materials
cards.note: It is often said to have overthrown vitalism, the idea that organic matter needs a life force, but historians dispute this.

cards.prompt: Discovered electromagnetic induction, generating a current from a changing magnetic field
cards.note: Joseph Henry observed induction independently in 1832, but Faraday published first; Faraday had begun as a bookbinder's apprentice.

cards.prompt: Measured the mechanical equivalent of heat with a paddle wheel driven by falling weights
cards.note: Julius Robert von Mayer proposed the equivalence of heat and work in 1842, sparking a priority dispute; Joule managed a brewery.

cards.prompt: Predicted the position of an unseen planet, Neptune, from irregularities in the orbit of Uranus
cards.note: Johann Galle found it at Berlin using Le Verrier's figures; John Couch Adams had calculated independently, sparking a priority dispute.

cards.prompt: Gave the first simple, direct demonstration of the Earth's rotation with a long pendulum
cards.note: His most famous pendulum hung a 28 kilogram bob on a 67 metre wire from the dome of the Panthéon in Paris.

cards.prompt: Traced a London cholera outbreak to a contaminated water pump on Broad Street
cards.note: Removing the pump handle is often credited with ending the outbreak, though Snow noted it may already have been declining.

cards.prompt: Jointly presented the theory of evolution by natural selection to the Linnean Society of London
cards.answer: Charles Darwin and Alfred Russel Wallace
cards.note: Wallace conceived the idea in the Malay Archipelago while in bed with a fever, then sent his essay to Darwin.

cards.prompt: Discovered caesium with their new technique of flame spectroscopy
cards.note: Found in Dürkheim mineral water, it was named from the Latin caesius, bluish grey, after its bright blue spectral lines.

cards.prompt: Unified electricity and magnetism and predicted that light is an electromagnetic wave
cards.note: Freeman Dyson called its publication the most important event of the nineteenth century in the history of the physical sciences.

cards.prompt: Discovered the basic laws of inheritance by breeding pea plants
cards.note: He twice failed the oral exam to become a certified teacher; his work was ignored until three botanists rediscovered it in 1900.

cards.prompt: Published a periodic table of the elements, leaving gaps for elements not yet discovered
cards.note: Lothar Meyer published a very similar table months later, but Mendeleev predicted the properties of gallium, scandium and germanium.

cards.prompt: Found no sign of the luminiferous aether in a precise interferometer experiment
cards.note: Their interferometer sat on a heavy sandstone slab floating in mercury, so it could be turned smoothly through every direction.

cards.prompt: First produced and detected radio waves, confirming Maxwell's electromagnetic theory
cards.note: Asked what his discovery could be used for, Hertz reportedly replied nothing; he also first noticed the photoelectric effect.

cards.prompt: Isolated argon from air, the first noble gas to be discovered
cards.note: Henry Cavendish had suspected an unreactive component of air in 1785; the name comes from the Greek for lazy or inactive.

cards.prompt: Discovered X-rays while experimenting with cathode-ray tubes
cards.note: On seeing an X-ray image of her own hand, his wife Anna Bertha reportedly exclaimed that she had seen her death.

cards.prompt: Discovered that uranium salts emit penetrating radiation without any need for sunlight
cards.note: Overcast Paris skies made him store his wrapped plates in a dark cabinet; developed anyway, they showed images just as sharp.

cards.prompt: Showed that cathode rays are streams of tiny negatively charged particles, discovering the electron
cards.note: Seven of his students won Nobel Prizes, and his son George later won one for showing that electrons behave as waves.

cards.prompt: Discovered the radioactive elements polonium and radium in uranium ore
cards.note: Polonium, found first, was named after Marie's homeland, Poland, which was then partitioned between Russia, Germany and Austria.

cards.prompt: Explained black-body radiation by assuming energy is emitted only in discrete quanta
cards.note: He later called his resort to quantisation an act of despair; he presented it to the German Physical Society on 14 December 1900.

cards.prompt: Explained the photoelectric effect by proposing that light comes in quanta of energy hf
cards.note: This, not relativity, was cited in his 1921 Nobel Prize; Millikan confirmed it while finding light particles quite unthinkable.

cards.prompt: Published the special theory of relativity, in On the Electrodynamics of Moving Bodies
cards.note: Written while he was a patent examiner in Bern, the paper has no references and names only five other scientists.

cards.prompt: Found that thin gold foil deflects a few alpha particles through more than 90 degrees
cards.note: Marsden was a 20-year-old undergraduate; in 1915 he moved to Wellington, New Zealand, as professor of physics at Victoria University College.

cards.prompt: Measured the charge of the electron by balancing charged oil droplets in an electric field
cards.note: Papers found after Fletcher's death suggest Millikan pressed him to give up authorship as a condition of receiving his PhD.

cards.prompt: Discovered superconductivity: mercury's electrical resistance vanished when cooled with liquid helium
cards.note: Three years earlier, in 1908, he had become the first person to liquefy helium, which made the discovery possible.

cards.prompt: Discovered cosmic rays by carrying electrometers to 5,300 metres in a balloon
cards.note: To rule out the Sun as the source, he made an ascent during a near-total solar eclipse; the radiation still rose with altitude.

cards.prompt: Discovered that a Cepheid variable star's period reveals its true brightness, a cosmic yardstick
cards.note: Gösta Mittag-Leffler tried to nominate her for a Nobel Prize in 1924, not knowing she had died three years earlier.

cards.prompt: Proposed that the continents slowly drift across the surface of the Earth
cards.note: Mainstream geology rejected the idea until the 1960s; Wegener died on the Greenland ice sheet in 1930, on his fourth expedition there.

cards.prompt: Explained hydrogen's spectral lines with electrons jumping between fixed orbits
cards.note: A keen footballer, he kept goal for Akademisk Boldklub; his brother Harald played for Denmark at the 1908 Olympics.

cards.prompt: Measured starlight bending around the Sun at the 1919 eclipse, confirming general relativity
cards.note: Eddington was a conscientious objector; Dyson supported his exemption from war service by proposing that he lead an eclipse expedition.

cards.prompt: Showed that X-rays lose energy when scattered by electrons, as if light were made of particles
cards.note: It won him the 1927 Nobel Prize; in the Second World War he oversaw the Manhattan Project's Metallurgical Laboratory.

cards.prompt: Proposed in his PhD thesis that electrons, and all matter, have wave properties
cards.note: He first took a degree in history before turning to physics; his Nobel Prize came after electron diffraction confirmed the idea.

cards.prompt: Showed in her PhD thesis that stars are made mostly of hydrogen and helium
cards.note: Henry Norris Russell called the result spurious, so she wrote it was almost certainly not real; he reached it himself four years later.

cards.prompt: Launched quantum mechanics with his 1925 reinterpretation paper, developed into matrix mechanics with Born and Jordan
cards.note: Suffering severe hay fever, he retreated to the pollen-free North Sea island of Helgoland, where the key ideas came together.

cards.prompt: Formulated the wave equation describing how a particle's quantum state evolves
cards.note: Peter Debye's offhand remark that waves should obey a wave equation prompted the work, worked out at a sanatorium in Arosa, Switzerland.

cards.prompt: Observed electrons diffracting off a nickel crystal, confirming that matter behaves as waves
cards.note: An accidental air leak forced them to heat their nickel target, which recrystallised into the large single crystals that diffracted electrons.

cards.prompt: Noticed a mould killing bacteria on a culture plate, discovering penicillin
cards.note: Turning penicillin into a usable drug fell largely to Howard Florey and Ernst Chain, who shared his 1945 Nobel Prize.

cards.prompt: Published evidence that galaxies recede at speeds proportional to their distance
cards.note: Georges Lemaître noted the same proportionality in 1927, which is why it is now officially called the Hubble-Lemaître law.

cards.prompt: Discovered the neutron, an uncharged particle in the atomic nucleus
cards.note: In Paris, Irène Joliot-Curie and Frédéric Joliot had seen the radiation knock protons from paraffin wax but assumed it was gamma rays.

cards.prompt: Found the positron, the first known antiparticle, in cosmic-ray tracks in a cloud chamber
cards.note: It confirmed Dirac's predicted anti-electron; Anderson later acknowledged inspiration from his Caltech classmate Chung-Yao Chao.

cards.prompt: Discovered from seismic waves that the Earth has a solid inner core
cards.note: A key clue came from waves of the 1929 Murchison earthquake in New Zealand reaching Russian stations where none were expected.

cards.prompt: Detected barium after bombarding uranium with neutrons, the chemical evidence for nuclear fission
cards.note: Lise Meitner and Otto Frisch explained it as the splitting of the nucleus and named it fission, but only Hahn received a Nobel.

cards.prompt: Led the first self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction, in a reactor beneath a Chicago stadium stand
cards.note: Chicago Pile-1 ran for about four and a half minutes at half a watt; Eugene Wigner celebrated with a bottle of Chianti.

cards.prompt: Invented the transistor at Bell Labs, starting with the point-contact transistor
cards.note: Bardeen later won a second Nobel Prize in Physics, for the theory of superconductivity, the only person to win it twice.

cards.prompt: Proposed the double-helix structure of DNA, with paired bases suggesting how genes are copied
cards.note: Their model relied on unpublished X-ray data from King's College London, including Rosalind Franklin's; she died in 1958, before the 1962 Nobel.

cards.prompt: First detected the neutrino, using antineutrinos streaming from a nuclear reactor
cards.note: Wolfgang Pauli had proposed the particle in 1930; Reines received a Nobel Prize in 1995, but Cowan had died in 1974.

cards.prompt: Showed that parity is not conserved in the weak interaction, using the beta decay of cobalt-60
cards.note: Tsung-Dao Lee and Chen-Ning Yang, who proposed the test, won the 1957 Nobel Prize; Wu herself was not included.

cards.prompt: Built the first working laser, using a synthetic ruby crystal
cards.note: Physical Review Letters rejected his paper, so he reported the invention in Nature; it built on laser theory by Townes and Schawlow.

cards.prompt: Proposed that protons and neutrons are built from smaller constituents he named quarks
cards.note: George Zweig independently proposed the same idea that year in a longer manuscript, calling the particles aces.

cards.prompt: Discovered the cosmic microwave background as unexplained noise in a horn antenna
cards.note: They evicted nesting pigeons and cleaned out droppings, but the noise remained; a Princeton group nearby was preparing to search for it.

cards.prompt: Spotted a bit of scruff on radio telescope chart paper: the first known pulsar
cards.note: The signal was nicknamed LGM-1, for little green men; the 1974 Nobel Prize recognising the discovery did not include her.

cards.prompt: Proposed that an asteroid impact killed the dinosaurs, from iridium in boundary clay
cards.note: A father-and-son team, a physicist and a geologist, they worked with chemists Frank Asaro and Helen Michel on the iridium measurements.

cards.prompt: Discovered buckminsterfullerene, a football-shaped molecule of sixty carbon atoms
cards.note: Named after the architect Buckminster Fuller, whose geodesic domes it resembles; the three shared the 1996 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

cards.prompt: Discovered the first planet orbiting a Sun-like main-sequence star, 51 Pegasi b
cards.note: The planet, a hot Jupiter, circles its star in about four days, far closer than Mercury is to the Sun.

cards.prompt: First created a Bose-Einstein condensate, using rubidium atoms cooled almost to absolute zero
cards.note: Wolfgang Ketterle at MIT produced one with sodium atoms later that year, and all three shared the 2001 Nobel Prize.

cards.prompt: Found from distant supernovae that the expansion of the universe is accelerating
cards.answer: Saul Perlmutter, Brian Schmidt and Adam Riess
cards.note: Two rival teams reached the result independently; cosmologists had expected the expansion to be slowing down under gravity.

cards.prompt: Isolated graphene, a single layer of carbon atoms, by peeling graphite with adhesive tape
cards.note: Geim had won an Ig Nobel Prize in 2000 for levitating a frog with magnetism; he is the only winner of both prizes.

cards.prompt: Showed that the bacterial CRISPR-Cas9 system can be programmed to cut chosen DNA sequences
cards.note: CRISPR sequences were first noticed by Yoshizumi Ishino in 1987; Doudna and Charpentier shared the 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

cards.prompt: Discovered the Higgs boson at CERN's Large Hadron Collider
cards.note: Peter Higgs and François Englert won the 2013 Nobel Prize for predicting it in 1964, in two of three independent teams.

cards.prompt: Made the first direct detection of gravitational waves, from two merging black holes
cards.note: The signal, GW150914, came from black holes of 36 and 29 solar masses; Einstein doubted such waves could ever be detected.
